A changed interface token, missing binding or host token, or mutable version declaration fails the public import and type assertions.
The package must expose all four public contract versions before any agent is constructed.
Malformed construction must fail by name; accepted construction immediately permits sessions and selected primary work.
Unknown construction fields must be refused with invalid_input and the offending field name; invalid supported choices cannot be silently ignored.
Duplicate tool names and absent handlers must fail during construction before any turn exists.
Both an extra providers field and an array supplied as provider must fail construction.
Agent, session, and turn model choices must equal turn_started.primary_actual and actual usage, while unknown selections fail by name.
Upward session, turn, and delegated selections must fail, while downward primary and delegated work uses the lower named model.
Concurrent agents must retain distinct model selections, callback identities, approval policies, ids, and result histories after mutation of the original options.
Generated ids must match lowercase UUIDv4 and supplied ids must accept exact length boundaries while refusing invalid characters, case, prefixes, and lengths.
Duplicate creation, unknown resume, and live durable resume/delete must return their distinct registered codes, including across independent agents.
Every closed ephemeral child or generated session must refuse resume with not_found.
Deletion must refuse a live handle, remove closed durable sessions from listing, and make later resume and repeated deletion fail not_found.
Forks must copy history, inherit persistence, generate a new id, isolate child turns, preserve transitive forks, and refuse a busy parent.
All four registered roles and multiple text parts must be accepted while tool/function roles, media parts, call structures, and malformed messages fail.
An empty seed with empty content must fail invalid_input and leave the first turn available.
Mutating accepted nested history must not change the recorded role, text, message order, or part boundaries.
History must be refused on durable sessions, after an accepted seed, and by forks inheriting conversation, while an unused ephemeral session accepts it.
Seeded input must still report closed or busy before attempting a new turn.
Four imported messages must create exactly one actual turn, retain the seed on its input, and generate only the current scripted usage.
The first seeded turn must be fresh and account for the current provider request without importing historical usage.
Turn identity must be frozen, nonempty, and equal every event identity; attempted mutation must fail.
run must equal the streamed terminal record and both paths must retain the accepted input and result in history.
A second consumer must fail stream_already_consumed during an active turn and after completion.
A consumer must receive output before a blocked provider settles and paused consumption must not block caller execution.
Engine loss must produce one failure or accepted-cancellation terminal after authoritative caller outcomes and reasoning drain.
Close must wait for active caller work and approval callbacks, retain paired resolutions, and prevent a late allow from starting an effect.
Repeated cancellation must remain harmless, prevent queued effects, drain nested or executing work, and preserve turn_cancelled after engine loss.
For caller, built-in, and MCP effects, deny/cancel/invalid/timeout/unavailable must produce their exact terminal state/code and execute no effect.
Non-allow and late timed-out approval decisions must produce no effects; close must ignore a later allow.
Every sequence must start at one and remain contiguous; reordered/missing sequence mutants and foreign session/turn identities must fail.
Every event carries the turn-events/1 envelope, registry or owned type, and a valid UTC timestamp if supplied; malformed timestamp/type mutants fail.
turn_started occurs once first, reports the actual primary selection, and distinguishes a fresh seed from resumed history.
Successful, failed, rejected, cancelled, and engine-loss traces require one first start and one last terminal; missing/duplicate-terminal mutants fail.
Each source call and approval must resolve exactly once after its matching request, including cancellation and engine loss; orphan correlation mutants fail.
Ordered output parts must equal terminal content and reasoning runs must equal their final text, including engine loss; altered delta/final mutants fail.
An owned event must preserve its exact type, nested payload ordering, unsafe integer, and owned envelope field without conversion or omission.
Success must omit an error, all other states must carry named errors, and accepted-turn cancellation must remain distinct from approval cancellation.
Recoverable tool_failed and tool_completion_unknown retain tool-result errors and allow success; stop/protocol/executor failures remain terminal failures.
Pre-stream invalid requests must reject their method while provider, tool, and approval failures after start must arrive in terminal records.
Public native errors must retain code/category/message/remedy/retryability, approval correlation ids, and exact uncertain-call details.
Distinct scripted primary/delegated counters must sum exactly, including unsafe integers and explicit zero cache counters; fabricated constants or rounding fail.
Known decimal cost must preserve its exact cumulative value, while unknown cost must remain absent from the ordinary usage record.
Every actual primary and delegated model must have its own exact usage entry; a rejected upward delegation must contribute no model entry.
Final cumulative usage must follow attributable work, immediately precede terminal in scripted traces, and equal terminal usage without losing delegated selections.
Every operation on a closed agent or session must fail closed; repeated close remains harmless and cannot reopen a handle.
An early runtime exit must reject public construction with a complete engine_unavailable error before agent or provider work begins.
A successful handshake advertising incompatible contract versions must fail public construction with contract_version_mismatch without advancing to agent.create.

Shared exact integers, decimals, Unicode, null/boolean/nested JSON, timestamps, callback deadlines, ids, content boundaries, and unknown envelope/payload/error fields must survive public binding translation.
Both bindings must match the same complete type-order literals for all eleven registered events, an owned event, resumed turns, and forked turns.
Both public bindings must retain identical complete shared errors for closed handles, method failures, and terminal failures, including exact remedies and owned fields.
Run, resume, and fork must match shared complete result and event-order literals; full record and error fixtures reject binding-specific values or dropped fields.
Changing instructions, models, tool declarations/schema/handlers, approvals, skill/MCP arrays, environment, or host files after construction cannot change later requests or newly created sessions.
Observed provider configuration must follow code over environment over file over defaults for provider/model/storage, preserve ambient workspace ownership, and remain captured after host mutation.
JSON booleans and exactly false/0/no strings must reach provider configuration as booleans; ambiguous strings, numeric values, null, lists, and maps fail with a field-specific remedy.
File and environment misspellings must be refused by name with their nearest registered key as the remedy.
A fresh Node host and fresh runtime must recover completed durable turns after every previous host/runtime exits, retaining history and resumed continuation.
Durable state must resume from its configured root and remain absent from another root, including across independent host processes.
Identical durable ids must remain isolated between workspaces; invalid slugs fail while minimum and maximum valid lengths are accepted.
A new request must contain earlier terminal replies, while a second active run/start and a busy fork fail immediately instead of queueing.
A blocked session cannot prevent independent progress or leak seeded conversation into another session; forks retain distinct histories.
Observed provider messages must retain seed order and parts, append one user message only for nonempty content, and avoid inventing a trailing user message.
Each later and forked provider request must contain the original seed and prior reply exactly once, without propagating mutations or sibling turns.
Historical system/developer text cannot replace configured instructions, remove the offered caller tool, or bypass a denying approval policy.
All registered payloads must retain their contracted fields; progress must be strict JSON, usage must be the exact replacement snapshot, and malformed progress mutants fail.
Unknown unqualified types must fail the observation validator while an owned success-like event or progress cannot replace a later failure terminal.
Observed native errors require registered or owned codes and registered categories; an unqualified invented error code must fail the same public-trace validator.
Caller arguments must remain decoded exact JSON, callback and event ids must correlate with approval ids, and the optional deadline must survive unchanged.

Reported failure, uncertain completion, callback exception, malformed result, mismatched correlation, and duplicate callback resolution retain distinct codes; invalid or unreachable callbacks cannot become recoverable under continue.

Five invalid policy values are rejected before observed provider work; mutating accepted options cannot change the omitted stop default; environment and file policy values are refused; explicit continue alone permits truthful recovery.
